we have developed a current spinning Hall magnetic sensor and its interface circuit, which is fabricated in a standard 0.18 μm CMOS technology.
the current-mode Hall magnetic sensors have been developed for high sensitivity, low power consumption, and low noise applications.

a magnetic sensor has been implemented in a CMOS technology, which has an offset of less than 50 µT (measured on 10 samples), a sensitivity of 166 V/A/mT, a bandwidth of 1 kHz and an input-referred noise of 2.5 µA/√Hz.

the design and implementation of a low-noisemagnetic sensor for automotive applications.
the development of a low-power, low-offset and high-sensitivity magnetic sensor for automotive applications.
the design and development of a low-nois CMOS current-mode sensor for low-frequency magnetic field measurement.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a current spinning technique can be used in combination with the current-mode Hall sensor, which allows a reduction in the offset and the bias current, while maintaining a high voltage sensitivity.
the current spinning technique, together with a low-noise amplifier, enables the design of low-power and low-noise Hall magnetic sensors.
the proposed Hall sensor has a very low bias current (12 μA) and high voltage sensitivity (1660 V/A/T) with low offset (50 μT) and low noise (1.2 μV/√Hz).

the presented sensor is able to detect a field of 1.5 mT at a sampling frequency of 25 kS/S.
a current-mode Hall magnetic field sensor with a low bias current and a high sensitivity front-end has been designed and fabricated in a standard CMOS technology and has been successfully tested.
the proposed Hall sensor is the best one among all the reported Hall sensors in terms of sensitivity, offset and power consumption.

the proposed current-mode Hall sensor can be used to measure magnetic fields as low as 0.5 μT with a bias current of 10 μA.
the current mode Hall sensor is a promising alternative to voltage mode Hall sensors.
